*Set up the R environment used in the tutorial, either via the workshop cloud environment or locally on your laptop.*

## Option A (recommended): Workshop RStudio environment

A virtual machine running RStudio Server in PDC Cloud is available during the workshop. You will get a link, a username and a password.

Resources are shared, so **avoid creating additional large objects**. The machine shuts down after the workshop, so save your work as an R script and download it via the Files pane (More → Export) before you leave.

### Check required packages

All required packages are pre-installed in the workshop environment. Load them and confirm that they are available:

```r
library(asvoccur)
library(duckplyr)
library(ecolongr)
library(vegan)
library(rworldmap)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
```

### Check access to example data {#check-access}

For this tutorial, ASV portal data is pre-downloaded and available on the virtual machine. It has also been prepared once for everyone, in shared folders called *stores*. Choose the data you want to work with and set the paths:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Insects

```r
data_path  <- "/srv/course-data/insects"
store_path <- "/srv/course-store/insects"
list.files(data_path)
```

If two (IBA_CO1) zip files are listed, you are ready to [proceed](tutorial-02-prep.qmd).

## Marine plankton

```r
data_path  <- "/srv/course-data/plankton"
store_path <- "/srv/course-store/plankton"
list.files(data_path)
```

If two (16S) zip files are listed, you are ready to [proceed](tutorial-02-prep.qmd).
:::

## Option B (fallback): Run RStudio locally on your laptop

You will need to install:

1. [R](https://cran.r-project.org/){target="_blank"}<br>
2. [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/){target="_blank"}
3. tools for compiling R packages, because `ecolongr` contains C++ code:
   - **macOS:** run `xcode-select --install` in the Terminal
   - **Windows:** [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/){target="_blank"}, in the version that matches your R
   - **Linux:** usually the `build-essential` and `r-base-dev` packages
4. the following R packages:
   - `remotes`
   - `asvoccur`
   - `duckplyr`
   - `ecolongr`
   - `vegan`
   - `rworldmap`
   - `lubridate`
   - `ggplot2`

To install and load the required R packages:

```r
# Install from CRAN
install.packages(c(
  "remotes",
  "duckplyr",
  "vegan",
  "rworldmap",
  "lubridate",
  "ggplot2"
))

# Install from GitHub
# The long-format functions are not yet in a release of asvoccur
remotes::install_github("biodiversitydata-se/asvoccur@feature/parquet-long-format")
remotes::install_github("biodiversitydata-se/ecolongr@0.1.1")

# Load
library(asvoccur)
library(duckplyr)
library(ecolongr)
library(vegan)
library(rworldmap)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)

# Confirm versions
"merge_long" %in% getNamespaceExports("asvoccur")  # Should say TRUE
packageVersion("ecolongr")  # Should say 0.1.1
```

### Download example data from the ASV portal

In this option, example data is downloaded directly from the ASV portal.

1. Go to the [ASV portal start page](https://asv-portal.biodiversitydata.se/index){target="_blank"}.

   Click **DOWNLOAD**. If you are not already logged in, you will be redirected to the login page.

2. If you do not already have an account, either:
   - sign in with a Google or GitHub account, or
   - create a new SBDI account.

3. On the **Download** page, under **Download link**, download the two datasets of the track you have chosen:

   - **Insects:** IBA_CO1_homogenate_2019_SE and IBA_CO1_lysate_2019_SE
   - **Marine plankton:** KTH-2013-Baltic-16S and PRJEB55296-16S

4. Place the two zip files in a folder of their own, e.g.:

       course-data/
       └── insects/
           ├── IBA_CO1_homogenate_2019_SE.zip
           └── IBA_CO1_lysate_2019_SE.zip

5. Set the paths in R and confirm access. The store is a new folder that is created in the next step:
```r
data_path  <- "local/path/to/course-data/insects"
store_path <- "local/path/to/course-store/insects"
list.files(data_path)
```

If the expected zip file(s) are listed, you are ready to [proceed](tutorial-02-prep.qmd).
